subject: health
essentialQuestion: What does respect look like in practice when a boundary is inconvenient for someone?

prompts.prompt: Explain characteristics of healthy, unhealthy, and coercive relationship patterns in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of setting, stating, and holding a personal boundary.
Apply consent as ongoing, informed, freely given, and revocable in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving recognizing pressure, manipulation, and control tactics; correct it and explain why.
Connect ending or stepping back from a relationship safely with where to go when a relationship stops being safe. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Build a boundary and consent script set for four fictional situations, including one where the boundary is not accepted the first time, and identify the exit and support step for each.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

adaptationChoices: Scripts may be written, typed, spoken privately to an adult, signed, or assembled from a supplied phrase bank. No role-play in front of an audience is required.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. No assessment requires disclosure, a recording, or any body measurement.
trustedAdultNote: Direct any urgent safety, health, or mental-health concern to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
